Ch.8 summary

AC recap

Formula sheet

a.c. \(\,I = I_0\sin\omega t\); \(V_{\rm rms}=V_0/\sqrt2\) (sine)

\(P = V_{\rm rms} I_{\rm rms}\) resistive

Ideal transformer: \(\dfrac{V_P}{V_S}=\dfrac{N_P}{N_S},\ I_P V_P\approx I_S V_S\)

High \(V\) → lower \(I\) → \(I^2R\) loss ↓; grid step-up/step-down

Common mistakes

rms vs peak

Heating uses rms, not peak; √2 only for sine. d.c. doesn't transform.

Power vs voltage

High V reduces loss for same delivered power; doesn't increase delivered power by itself.

Visual comparison

QuantityExpressionWhen it applies
DefinitionSee formula sheet aboveAlways: definitions are not the special case.
Special caseLinear / uniform limit (Ohm, uniform E/B, ideal transformer)Only when the conditions (constant T, large plates, long solenoid, ideal core) hold.

Quick check

Which statement best fits this chapter's theme?

B. Definitions (R=V/I, E=F/q, Φ=BAcosθ) hold generally; laws like Ohm, uniform E=V/d, ideal transformer are conditional. A confuses uniform vs non-uniform; C ignores R load; D swaps Lenz (direction) with Faraday (magnitude).
